direction.quote: MicroBooNE will be exposed to the 0.5-2 GeV on-axis Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB) at a ~500 m baseline, the same as was employed for MiniBoonE.
direction.value: on-axis toward the short-baseline detector halls on the Fermilab site, about 500 m from the target

intervals.label: operating
intervals.note: Evidence date only: the MiniBooNE flux paper (submitted June 2008) describes the BNB in routine operation for MiniBooNE. No source consulted (checked 2026-09-16) confirms the BNB first-beam date (commonly given as 2002).

name: Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB)
notes: The BNB start date (2002) is not sourced; see the interval note.

Short-baseline detector baselines are not recorded: SBND, MicroBooNE and ICARUS all sit on site:fermilab-main-campus, the same campus point as the beamline, so no site-to-site distance exists. Sourced figures for when separate detector sites exist (SBN proposal, arXiv:1503.01520, src:sbn-proposal-2015): SBND (then LAr1-ND) "will be located 110 m from the BNB target"; MicroBooNE "is located in the Liquid Argon Test Facility (LArTF) at 470 m"; the ICARUS T600 "will be located 600 m from the BNB target". SBND's own detector paper (arXiv:2504.00245) gives "located 110 meters from the Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB) target at Fermilab".

primary_beam.quote: protons with 8 GeV kinetic energy (8.89 GeV/c momentum)

energy.quote: The Booster delivers protons with 8 GeV kinetic energy (8.89 GeV/c momentum) to a beryllium target

secondary_beam.quote: Secondary mesons produced by the interaction of the protons in the target decay to produce a neutrino beam with an average energy of ∼ 800 MeV
secondary_beam.value: muon neutrinos / antineutrinos, on-axis, mean energy about 800 MeV

peak_neutrino_energy.note: Average, not peak, neutrino energy as stated by the source.
peak_neutrino_energy.quote: a neutrino beam with an average energy of ∼ 800 MeV

proton_energy.quote: protons with 8 GeV kinetic energy (8.89 GeV/c momentum)

summary.plain: A low-energy neutrino beam at Fermilab made by firing 8-billion-electronvolt protons at a beryllium target. It feeds the short-baseline detectors on the laboratory site.
summary.technical: On-axis muon-neutrino beam from 8 GeV kinetic (8.89 GeV/c) Booster protons on a beryllium target inside a pulsed horn, mean neutrino energy about 800 MeV, serving MiniBooNE, MicroBooNE, SBND and ICARUS at baselines of order 500 m.

target.quote: The Booster Neutrino Beamline (BNB) produces neutrinos using 8.89 GeV/c momentum protons from the Booster synchrotron that are incident on a beryllium target.
